expected_points: Use populatedGroup.get(childKey) to search its child fieldGroup and return the matching FormlyFieldConfig.
Angular form/control lookup targets an AbstractControl; the found field instead exposes its associated formControl.
limits: No universal equality of path semantics or return types; search is descendant-only.
Lookup behavior here is bounded to string or dot-joined array paths and traversed keyed groups with string/array keys; scalar numeric request or child-key traversal is not qualified.

expected_points: Use a dotted path relative to the populated group, e.g. group.get("address.city"); array requests are joined with dots. Matching keyed group prefixes are consumed during recursion.
An absent descendant yields undefined, not a control.
limits: Array segments containing dots collapse to the same lookup string; bracket notation is not normalized by this lookup.
Lookup behavior here is bounded to string or dot-joined array paths and traversed keyed groups with string/array keys; scalar numeric request or child-key traversal is not qualified.

expected_points: key "profile.email" identifies model data through the field key path.
id "email-editor" is the HTML identifier; name "contactEmail" is separately configured for the element name, not the model path.
limits: DOM application depends on formlyAttributes/template bindings; identifier and name do not override key.

expected_points: A supplied nonempty id is retained by getFieldId and applied by the ordinary single-element formlyAttributes path.
name is optional; this initialization does not generate a name from id or key, and formlyAttributes sets name only when field.name is truthy. Model association remains key.
limits: Do not promise universal DOM absence of name: a template or other configuration can supply it. Explicit directive id and multiple attached elements have separate handling.

expected_points: Input className binds to its outer formly-field host.
Group fieldGroupClassName binds to the built-in formly-group host.
limits: Neither is a direct native-input class binding.

expected_points: className applies to the outer formly-field of the group; fieldGroupClassName applies to its built-in formly-group component.
Neither automatically copies the class to every native input; descendant CSS effects depend on selectors and templates.
limits: Custom group templates must provide any desired class bindings.

expected_points: FieldTypeConfig<T> extends FormlyFieldConfig<T> with required formControl: FormControl and props: NonNullable<T>.
General FormlyFieldConfig has optional AbstractControl formControl and optional props; FieldType<FieldTypeConfig> narrows the custom scalar type surface.
These are TypeScript declarations, not proof of successful runtime field population.
FieldArrayTypeConfig<T> extends FormlyFieldConfig<T>, requires FormArray formControl and nonnullable props, and is the default configuration generic for FieldArrayType.
Scalar FieldTypeConfig instead requires FormControl; typing does not validate arbitrary runtime structures.
model returns this.field.model.
formControl returns this.field.formControl with a nonnullable type assertion.
props returns this.field.props or an empty object fallback.
limits: These accessors delegate to the populated field; model is not unconditionally the root model.

expected_points: options.formState carries shared form context separate from field model data.
A modern expression callback receives field and can access field.options.formState; a string expression has the formState binding.
limits: No automatic serialization or submission of formState is implied.

expected_points: options.build(field?) is declared to return FormlyFieldConfig; the builder-installed default builds the supplied field, defaults an omitted argument to the root, and returns that field.
options.checkExpressions(field) takes a field and evaluates its expressions.
limits: A caller-provided build callback is preserved. No entire lifecycle ordering or arbitrary control-preservation guarantee is required or established.

expected_points: options.detectChanges(field) checks expressions and marks relevant components, including descendants through the implementation traversal.
options.updateInitialValue(model?) stores a cloned reset baseline; an omitted/nullish model argument uses the current root field model.
Neither hook submits application model data.
limits: After-build exposed callbacks only; no application submission protocol is supplied.

expected_points: With registered wrappers ["frame", "caption"], frame is outer and caption is inner; the field type renders inside the remaining insertion target.
limits: Assumes functioning wrapper fieldComponent insertion targets.

expected_points: An explicit field wrappers array is retained, including []; registered type wrappers are copied only when field.wrappers is falsy after default merges.
The two arrays are not concatenated by this default-filling path.
When field wrappers are absent, earlier defaultOptions merges can supply them; if still falsy, getMergedField copies registered type wrappers.
The selected array renders first wrapper outermost and subsequent wrappers inward.
limits: Do not ignore defaults that supply wrappers before the registered-wrapper fallback.

expected_points: Later own component replaces the previous component; an omitted defaultOptions property leaves the earlier registry value intact.
getType returns the effective stored entry after inherited falsy component/wrapper filling.
limits: Order is processed registration-call order; no universal Angular module order or live-instance replacement is promised.

expected_points: setWrapper replaces the whole entry under that name; getWrapper(name) returns the later registration and therefore its component.
limits: Registry lookup only, not hot replacement of previously created components.

expected_points: setValidator replaces the named registry object; getValidator(name).validation is the later registered function.
A field-local validator expression/function is a separate configuration path, not another write to this registry.
limits: Already installed control validators are not automatically guaranteed to recompose.

expected_points: Types preserve omitted properties and replace supplied own component/extends/defaultOptions/wrappers properties.
Wrappers replace the whole named registry entry.
Validators replace the whole named registry entry.
limits: No single deep-merge rule applies to all three; order refers to actual calls on the instance.

expected_points: getType(name) returns null for an unknown string by default; getType(name, true) throws.
getWrapper(name) throws for an unknown string name and exposes no analogous suppress-throw flag.
limits: Type rendering requests getType with throwing enabled; nonthrowing registry lookup does not make an unregistered field renderable.

expected_points: For compatible ordinary props objects, a nonblank explicit field label is preserved and the omitted required value is filled from the preset.
If the explicit label is null, undefined or empty string, reverse merging fills it from the preset instead.
limits: Question does not specify a label value; do not silently assume every explicitly present value wins. Recursive merging requires matching object prototypes and excludes arrays.

expected_points: The explicit props.required=false survives preset required=true: false is not null, undefined or empty string.
limits: This concerns configuration merge, not a universal application validation policy.

expected_points: A different nonblank scalar field defaultValue wins over the preset defaultValue. Null, undefined or empty string can instead be default-filled; compatible object values can merge and existing arrays are retained.
Resolving defaultValue configuration is separate from model initialization: defaultValue only fills eligible undefined keyed model data and does not overwrite an already supplied model value.
limits: Question does not specify the values or their shapes, so unconditional replacement precedence would overstate the source.

expected_points: For an absent preset, substitution makes no assignment and leaves the #name type unresolved; it invents no fallback configuration.
On the ordinary render path, lookup of that unregistered #name type throws.
limits: Assumes #name is also not independently registered as a literal ordinary type. The preset extension itself does not directly throw.

expected_points: Set expressions.hide to a callback such as field => !!field.options.formState.hideEmail, or a supported formState string expression.
Set resetOnHide:false on the keyed field to skip model-value clearing when hidden.
limits: Hidden controls may still leave the active form control tree.

expected_points: A custom FieldArrayType subclass can call add() to append, or add(index, initialModel?, options?) to insert.
Call remove(index, options?) to remove a row; these methods coordinate model/fields/control registration and rebuilding.
limits: The APIs do not qualify arbitrary drag-and-drop reordering or guarantee control/subscription identity preservation. Example-defined repeat registration is not a built-in universal name.

expected_points: Extend FieldWrapper and expose its fieldComponent insertion target, typically a template container referenced as #fieldComponent.
Register wrappers:[{name:"frame",component:FrameWrapper}] through Formly configuration, and reference wrappers:["frame"] on the field.
limits: A wrapper does not substitute for a missing field renderer/control/value accessor.

expected_points: Register validators:[{name:"rule",validation:fn}] and use field.validators.validation:["rule"]. For typed Angular-style validation, fn returns null when valid or an error map such as {rule:true} when invalid.
Configure the actual error key rule in field.validation.messages or global validationMessages with name:"rule".
limits: Named field expression slots use boolean validity instead; message configuration is separate from visibility and custom wrapper rendering.

expected_points: For the Material select, set props.valueProp:"code" and props.labelProp:"title" alongside props.options.
The shared options pipe maps stored values and display labels separately.
limits: Mapping does not define object identity comparison; no native-select or other-adapter equivalence is required.

expected_points: Use field type:"input" with props.type:"number".
Formly type selects the renderer while props.type selects the HTML input kind; Material has a number template branch.
limits: Do not infer numeric parsing, locale, precision or serialization guarantees.

expected_points: Call FormlyJsonschema.toFieldConfig({type:"object",properties:{text:{type:"string"}}}) to obtain one FormlyFieldConfig.
For formly-form fields, place that return value in an outer fields array.
limits: Conversion does not register missing object/string renderers, qualify a turnkey Material application or establish full JSON Schema conformance.

expected_points: Set type:"radio" and props.options to two objects such as [{label:"First",value:"a"},{label:"Second",value:"b"}].
Material radio maps options through formlySelectOptions, displays option.label and binds each stored option.value separately.
limits: No browser/accessibility or object-equality guarantee beyond the renderer bindings.

expected_points: Do not qualify Formly 7.0.0 using evidence pinned to 6.3.12; any 6.3.12 explanation must be explicitly outside the requested version.
limits: Applicability is exact 6.3.12 across this batch and baseline catalog.

expected_points: Do not use Material renderer evidence to confirm Bootstrap native-input rendering; mark the requested adapter behavior unsupported by this evidence.
limits: Core contracts may be shared but do not prove a different adapter template.

expected_points: No definitive application diagnosis follows without application code or traces.
Request relevant field/model updates, HTTP-response handler, reproduction and timing/error trace for caller-side investigation.
limits: Do not invent application state or a particular root cause.

Any explanation of checkExpressions/detectChanges must remain bounded to the supplied Formly mechanisms.
limits: One library mechanism does not guarantee all custom component and expression updates.

expected_points: Reject automatic class propagation to all nested native inputs.
If explaining the bounded target, className is on formly-field, not a universal native-descendant binding.
limits: Custom wrappers/templates and CSS determine their own descendant effects.

Any path comparison must retain field-tree lookup limits, including dot joining and lack of bracket normalization.
limits: No exhaustive Angular path policy is needed to reject universal equivalence.

expected_points: Do not promise arbitrary reorder preservation of control identity, subscriptions or validity state.
If discussing supported alternatives, limit them to the documented add/remove coordination.
limits: Bounded add/remove behavior does not prove the requested reorder guarantee.

limits: No all-custom or all-async ordering follows from these separate mechanisms.
